aliases: Feng Huang Dancong You Hua Xiang
processing: Partially oxidised by withering and tossing, then fixed, rolled and dried, as with other Dancong. The pomelo-flower scent is natural to the leaf, not added.
harvest_season: Usually spring, as with most Fenghuang Dancong.
appearance_dry: Tight, plump strips, grey-brown with an oily sheen.
appearance_wet: Typically thick leaves with reddened edges, as with other tossed Dancong.
taste_profile: A natural pomelo-blossom scent that is high and long, on a sweet, brisk and mellow body. It keeps giving over many steeps.

brewing.notes: A preheated gaiwan and short pours keep the blossom note in focus.

vintage_note: As is usual for Dancong, it is sold by harvest year and season, mostly fresh spring tea or tea rested a year or two after roasting. The name refers to an aroma, so it may cover more than one tree: ask the seller what stands behind it.
description:
You Hua Xiang is the Dancong named after pomelo flowers. Chinese writers mention it among the Fenghuang strains and aromas beyond the ten best-known aroma types, though some lists include it among those ten.

The method is ordinary Dancong work: withering, tossing, fixing, rolling and drying. Like other Dancong, the scent comes from the leaf and the handling, so a perfumed nose with little taste behind it is a warning sign.

The finished tea has plump grey-brown strips, an orange-yellow liquor and a high, long blossom scent over a sweet, mellow body. It takes repeated steeping well.

When buying, smell the wet leaf and taste beyond the first cup. A true aroma should carry into the later steeps, not vanish after one or two.
history: Little is documented about the origin of this tea or who first selected it. It appears in Chinese accounts of Fenghuang Dancong aroma types, named simply for its scent, and is sold abroad as well under the same name.
